fresh_target_repo_state.main_note: SQLite V5 release identity policy and upstream-of-shell trust-boundary repair are merged; F-V01-13 remains unclosed.

observed_reality.claim_boundary: Absence of an explicit WAL-reset patch marker in the published Debian patch series is not by itself a universal proof about every possible binary-level backport; release remains fail-closed until exact fixed-runtime evidence exists.

live_external_evidence.claim_used: The WAL-reset corruption bug affects upstream SQLite 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3+, with specific backport releases also identified by upstream.
SQLite 3.53.4 is an upstream fixed-line release dated 2026-07-24 and supplies the source identity used by the current Frank V5 release policy.

grf.leading_generated_reality: Provision one independently pinned fixed SQLite artifact into a deployment-owned content-addressed runtime prefix, verify it before commit, and publish the V5 root anchor only after the runtime commit is durable.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: A self-consistent root anchor can still be unsafe if the manifest authorizes itself, deployment authority is compromised, service-manager startup binds a different loader environment/path, or rollback restores older installed state.

go_oob_experiment.baseline: content-identical anchor under root-owned non-group/world-writable parent chain accepted by V5 anchor trust checks
go_oob_experiment.intervention: same anchor content changed to UID/GID 1000; separate /tmp parent-chain sensitivity control also exercised
go_oob_experiment.interpretation: supports the current V5 root-owned parent-chain trust condition against ordinary Frank self-forging; does not establish protection against privileged deployment compromise or namespace/kernel attacks
